author_disclosure: Author-prepared by the project's AI coding assistant from the blind inputs only, for the user's review. Not an independent or expert credit review. The author had read the actual amendment descriptions while building the evaluator collection, so these judgments are not blind to the lender's history. Unlike the first two histories, no model output for this company existed when they were written.

rubric.reconsideration: warranted = evidence available at the cutoff gives a lender a supported reason to open a package review or make a targeted information request; unwarranted = routine monitoring is the defensible response; unresolved = the evidence raises a question public inputs cannot settle.
rubric.acceptable_actions: More than one action can be defensible. An information request is not an unnecessary escalation when a covenant input is unobservable.
rubric.not_scored: Exact thresholds, exact wording, or similarity to the actual amendment.

baseline: Original January 17, 2018 package: a First Lien Net Leverage Ratio schedule stepping from 4.00x in 2018 to 3.00x from September 2020, annual, quarterly and monthly statements with Compliance Certificates, notice duties, and restrictions on indebtedness. Contractual Consolidated EBITDA is not the company's public Adjusted EBITDA, so the ratio cannot be calculated from these reports.
character_of_history: A growth history. The lender's actual responses were driven by acquisitions and financing actions, not by deterioration. This history mainly tests restraint: whether ordinary strong quarters are left alone, and whether a large acquisition is recognized as a reason to revisit a package written for a much smaller borrower.

checkpoints.why: Full-year 2017 Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $22.3 million. The VIP acquisition this loan financed had just closed. Nothing departs from origination.

First quarter with VIP: net sales up 71.7%, Adjusted EBITDA $5.4 million against guidance of $5.0 million, full-year guidance of $40 to $45 million reaffirmed. Long-term debt of $126.9 million reflects the acquisition financing known at origination.
unsupported_if_claimed: that the rise in debt since year end is new information: it is the acquisition financing

checkpoints.why: Record sales, Adjusted EBITDA of $15.8 million, debt paid down to $107.4 million, liquidity increased. The revolver amendment concerns the separate bank facility.
unsupported_if_claimed: that the revolver amendment is a change to this term loan

checkpoints.why: Net sales up 117%, Adjusted EBITDA $13.4 million with margin expansion. A small $3.0 million acquisition is within ordinary course.
Record year, $73.9 million of new equity raised, cash of $66.4 million. Leverage pressure is falling, not rising. This is the history's clearest no-escalation checkpoint.

The company announced a $185 million cash acquisition of Perrigo Animal Health and cites pro forma net leverage. That is more than twice the size of the original $75 million loan. The indebtedness restrictions and the leverage schedule were written for a much smaller borrower, so the package needs revisiting before closing, whatever the operating results.
affected_themes: scale and leverage the package was written for
acceptable_actions: open a package review of indebtedness restrictions and the leverage schedule
request the pro forma covenant calculation and financing plan
unsupported_if_claimed: that operating performance has weakened: it has not

checkpoints.why: The acquisition closed and the company gives estimated net debt of $262 million after it, against about $100 million before. The original leverage schedule steps down to 3.50x within months. Operating results are strong; the capital structure the package assumed no longer exists.
affected_themes: scale and leverage the package was written for
acceptable_actions: package review of the leverage schedule and debt permissions
unsupported_if_claimed: a breach: the contractual ratio cannot be computed
checkpoints.dependence: Net debt after the acquisition reflects a hidden lender response.

checkpoints.why: Sales up 42% but a net loss of $8.8 million from $12.0 million of acquisition and integration costs, with the higher debt load in place. Whether leverage fits the original schedule cannot be judged from public figures.

A full-year net loss with $2.7 million of incremental interest, and a second acquisition pending: Capstar for about $95 million. Another debt-funded purchase on top of the 2019 one is a supported reason to revisit debt permissions and leverage headroom.
affected_themes: scale and leverage the package was written for
acceptable_actions: request the financing plan and covenant calculation

checkpoints.why: All clinics closed from March 20, 2020, 27 planned openings postponed, annual guidance suspended and the revolver drawn as a precaution. One of two segments has stopped operating. That warrants at least a targeted information request on liquidity and covenant headroom.
acceptable_actions: request a liquidity forecast and covenant calculation
unsupported_if_claimed: that the Products segment is impaired: it grew

checkpoints.why: Record sales and Adjusted EBITDA up 35.9% with Services revenue near zero, while long-term debt reached $357.8 million including new convertible debt. Operations are strong and the capital structure has changed again. Mixed.
affected_themes: scale and leverage the package was written for
checkpoints.dependence: The convertible debt was permitted by a hidden lender response.
